This report constructs a dimensionally consistent, falsifiable comparison between two maximal-information-processing systems whose "hardware" is constrained by physics in very different ways: (i) **cortical tissue**, whose sustained computation rate is bounded from below by the Landauer erasure cost per bit, W = k_B T ln 2, and from above by the Bremermann mass-energy throughput limit; and (ii) **cosmic-web gravitational collapse**, which can be viewed (in the mainstream ΛCDM picture) as a dissipative structure whose free-energy budget is bounded by the dark-matter halo binding energy and whose "information channel capacity" is limited by the Hubble flow and the phase-space density floors of dark matter.

The core quantitative results are:

## 2. Background, Motivation & Empirical Gaps

### 2.1 The Landauer–Bremermann program in biology

The Landauer principle [2,3] states that erasing one bit of information from a physical memory at temperature T requires, at minimum, the dissipation of W = k_B T ln 2 of free energy into heat. Bormashenko [2] reformulated this as a *mass-energy* statement: erasing one bit creates a minimal "recordable mass" m̃₀ = k_B T ln 2 / c² — information is physically anchored to gravitational mass. Herrera [4] extended this to general relativity, showing that Landauer's principle has a covariant formulation in curved spacetime, which is the mathematical prerequisite for comparing a biological (≈ 310 K, low-gravity) system with a cosmological (≈ expanding, high-gravity) one on the same footing.

The Bremermann limit is the complementary *throughput* bound: for a system of mass m, the maximum rate at which information can be (re)processed is bounded by the maximum rate at which mass-energy can be converted and dissipated, R_max ∝ mc²/(πħ) (the exact prefactor depends on the convention used — see §3.3). The two bounds together form a two-sided constraint on any physical information-processing device: the Landauer bound constrains *cost per bit*, the Bremermann bound constrains *bits per second per unit mass*.

**Empirical gap 1**: There is no published, dimensionally consistent comparison that treats cortical tissue and cosmic-web collapse as members of the same class of "dissipative information processors." This report fills that gap.

**Empirical gap 2**: The 35:1 communication:computation energy ratio reported by Levy & Calvert [1] is a *model-dependent* decomposition of the ~20 W human brain budget. It has not been independently cross-validated against electrophysiological measurements in other species, and the definition of "computation" vs. "communication" at the synaptic level is not unique. This is a direct falsification target.

**Empirical gap 3**: Karbowski [7] quantifies the energetic cost of synaptic plasticity (the *storage* operation), which is distinct from both communication and computation — yet is the operation most directly analogous to writing new information into the cosmic-web's "memory" (i.e., into the halo mass function and the cosmic-web filaments). No unified framework currently connects these.

### 2.2 The cosmological side: dissipation and information in gravitational collapse

Mainstream ΛCDM treats the cosmic web as a hierarchical, gravitational-collapse network whose "dissipation" is dominated by (i) virialization in dark-matter halos, (ii) baryonic cooling in galaxy clusters, and (iii) tidal stripping in filaments. In an information-theoretic framing (which is *not* standard ΛCDM but a *model-dependent overlay* that this report makes explicit), the cosmic web can be viewed as a low-throughput but enormous-capacity information processor: each halo virialization event irreversibly "erases" pre-collapse phase-space information, dissipating gravitational binding energy in the process — analogous to a Landauer erasure but at cosmological temperatures and scales.

**Observational tensions relevant to this comparison:**

   - Planck vs. KiDS: **2.809 σ, Δχ² = 7.89** (1 d.o.f., ρ = 0 assumption).
   - Planck vs. DES: **2.62 σ, Δχ² ≈ 5.6** (1 d.o.f., ρ = 0 assumption).

   - This tension is directly relevant to the "information processing" framing because it constrains how efficiently early-universe perturbations were *erased* by late-time nonlinear structure formation. If the erasure efficiency implied by ΛCDM is too high (as the S_8 tension suggests), the bound on gravitational information processing is violated — either the bound is wrong, or the model is wrong.

2. **JWST high-redshift anomalies**: JWST/NIRSpec has spectroscopically confirmed galaxies out to z = 14.32 (JADES-GS-z14-0, M_UV = −20.81 ± 0.16, ~290 Myr after the Big Bang [8]). ### 2.3 The alternative counter-hypothesis: Milgromian (MOND) structure formation

As a counter-hypothesis to ΛCDM, we use **Milgromian dynamics (MOND)** hydrodynamical structure formation [14], which replaces particle dark matter with a modification to Newtonian gravity. In the information-theoretic framing, this changes the *dissipation budget* fundamentally: without dark matter, the gravitational potential well depth at a given scale is set by the baryonic mass alone, so the "erasure" efficiency of gravitational collapse is *higher* (less binding energy is available to be dissipated), and the S_8 amplitude is predicted to be *lower* — potentially resolving the S_8 tension without invoking new physics in the early universe. Wittenburg et al. [14] show that Milgromian hydrodynamical simulations produce a cosmic web that is morphologically similar to ΛCDM but with different halo mass functions and different filament dynamics.

**Falsifiable prediction of the counter-hypothesis**: MOND predicts a specific relationship between the baryonic Tully–Fisher relation and the halo mass function that is *not* predicted by ΛCDM. If future Euclid/Rubin weak-lensing data confirm the ΛCDM-predicted S_8 amplitude (0.832) and simultaneously confirm the JWST high-z UV luminosity excess as being resolved by *baryonic* physics (not by dark-matter modifications), then the Milgromian counter-hypothesis is disfavored and the "gravitational-collapse-as-dissipative-processor" null model (which is ΛCDM-based) is tightened.

### 3.2 Validity Domain, Identification & Claim Scope

**Null-model conditions / identification assumptions:**

1. **[GENERAL]** The Landauer bound E_bit = k_B T ln 2 is a *lower* bound on the dissipation per irreversible bit-erasure, valid for any physical memory operating at temperature T, under the assumption of a quasistatic, reversible-to-irreversible transition. This is a theorem-level result in quantum statistical mechanics [2,3] and is not model-dependent on a particular hardware implementation.
2. **[MODEL-DEPENDENT: assumption that cortical information processing is predominantly "erasure-like"]** The identification of neural computation with bit-erasure is an *interpretive assumption*, not a theorem. A neural spike train may carry information without erasing it; the Landauer bound applies only to the *irreversible* component. Levy & Calvert [1] show that only a small fraction of the ~20 W budget goes to "computation" proper (~35× less than communication), so the effective Landauer-limited erasure rate is much smaller than the naive P_brain/E_bit ceiling. This is a direct falsification target: if future electrophysiology shows that the "communication" component is actually irreversible-erasure in nature, the ratio must be revised.
3. **[MODEL-DEPENDENT: assumption of a well-defined "virialization temperature" T_vir(M, z) for each halo]** The cosmological "erasure temperature" is not uniquely defined; we adopt the standard virial temperature relation T_vir ∝ M^(2/3)(1+z) for a halo of mass M at redshift z, under the assumption of a ΛCDM-predicted halo mass function. Under the Milgromian counter-hypothesis, this relation is modified, and the denominator of the estimand changes.
4. **[GENERAL]** The Gaussian tension calculation, tension_σ = |val₁ − val₂| / √(err₁² + err₂² − 2·ρ_corr·err₁·err₂), is a valid approximation when both measurements are approximately Gaussian-distributed and their joint covariance is known or bounded. This is a standard statistical result, not model-dependent on the underlying cosmology.
5. **[MODEL-DEPENDENT: assumption that the "cosmic-web information channel" has a finite capacity set by the horizon]** This is an *interpretive* assumption. It is motivated by the fact that the Hubble flow (H_0 = 2.1331 × 10⁻⁴² · h GeV in canonical units) sets the maximum rate at which new causal information can enter the observable universe, but the "capacity" language is a *metaphor* mapped onto the cosmological constant problem. It is **not** [GENERAL]; it is explicitly flagged as a model-dependent overlay.
6. **[GENERAL]** The identification of JWST high-z excess (log₁₀ ρ_UV = 25.1 ± 0.2 at z ≈ 12, i.e., 3–10× above the fiducial ΛCDM prediction with ε* ≤ 0.15–0.20) as an *observational tension* is robust — it is a direct measurement vs. a model prediction, and the discrepancy is 3–10× (not marginal). However, the *interpretation* of this excess (feedback-free star formation, top-heavy Pop III IMF, direct-collapse BH seeds, enhanced small-scale power, Early Dark Energy, MOND) is **[MODEL-DEPENDENT]** and is an open research question [9,10,11].
